journey.title: Tab away after typing an unavailable delivery date
journey.goal: Leaving the date field with Tab closes the calendar even when the typed date is outside the delivery window

steps.title: Type a date outside the delivery window

functionalJourney.title: Move the delivery into June with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking through the calendar to June and choosing a day fills the delivery date

guards.title: Type a valid delivery date and Tab away
guards.goal: A correctly typed date is committed and the calendar closes when the user tabs away

plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not hide on blur when the entered date is outside the allowed range because there is no blur event listener to close the calendar; the existing hide logic is tied to validation or explicit hide calls that are not triggered on Tab away.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field in non-inline mode that calls datepicker.hide(), ensuring the calendar closes when the user tabs away regardless of date validity.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can reliably close the datepicker by tabbing out of the field, preventing unexpected focus trapping and satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: The datepicker will hide on blur even if the user intends to correct an invalid date; however the requirement specifies that Tab away should close the calendar regardless of validity.
Inline pickers are unaffected because the listener is added only in the non‑inline branch.
If other code depends on the blur event to keep the picker open for custom validation, that behavior will change; but the datepicker's own validation already runs on input change.
verification_requirements: After typing a valid or invalid date and pressing Tab, the datepicker element must not be visible.
Clicking outside the picker should still hide it.
Inline pickers must remain visible when their host element receives blur.
Selecting a date via the mouse grid should still update the field and hide the picker if configured.
The blur listener should not cause duplicate hide calls or errors.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not hide on blur when the user tabs away because there is no blur event listener attached to the input field in non-inline mode. Additionally, the exitEditMode method has a logic error: it returns early when editMode is true, preventing proper cleanup of edit mode state, which may contribute to unexpected input field behavior.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field in the non-inline branch that calls datepicker.hide(). Also fix the exitEditMode condition so it actually exits edit mode when editMode is true, ensuring the input field is not left in an inconsistent state.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can reliably close the datepicker by tabbing out of the field, preventing unexpected focus trapping and satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order). The edit mode cleanup fix ensures the input field does not retain stale editing state.
functional_risks: The datepicker will hide on blur even if the user intends to correct an invalid date; however the requirement specifies that Tab away should close the calendar regardless of validity.
Inline pickers are unaffected because the listener is added only in the non-inline branch.

Fixing the exitEditMode condition changes behavior when the picker is hidden while in edit mode; it will now properly exit edit mode instead of leaving the input field in edit mode. This should not break existing flows because the picker is being hidden anyway.
verification_requirements: After typing a valid or invalid date and pressing Tab, the datepicker element must not be visible.
Clicking outside the picker should still hide it.
Inline pickers must remain visible when their host element receives blur.
Selecting a date via the mouse grid should still update the field and hide the picker if configured.
The blur listener should not cause duplicate hide calls or errors.
The regression guard 'Type a valid delivery date and Tab away' must hold with form-data reflecting the typed valid date.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker does not update its selection when the user tabs away from the input field because there is no blur event listener that triggers validation and selection update. The existing blur listener (added in a previous attempt) only hides the picker without updating the selection, so the input field reverts to the previous valid date and the form data does not reflect the newly typed date.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a blur event listener to the input field in the non-inline branch that calls the datepicker's update() method. This method reads the input field value, validates it, updates the selection if valid (or reverts if invalid), and hides the picker (autohide defaults to true in update). This ensures the calendar closes on Tab and the form data reflects the typed date for valid entries.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Keyboard users can reliably close the datepicker by tabbing out of the field, and the datepicker will update the selection with the typed date (if valid) or revert to the last valid date (if invalid), satisfying WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 2.4.3 (Focus Order).
functional_risks: The datepicker will update on blur even if the user intends to correct an invalid date; however the requirement specifies that Tab away should close the calendar and update the selection.
Inline pickers are unaffected because the listener is added only in the non-inline branch.
If other code depends on the blur event to keep the picker open for custom validation, that behavior will change; but the datepicker's own validation already runs on input change.
verification_requirements: After typing a valid date (e.g., 2024-05-21) and pressing Tab, the datepicker element must not be visible and the form data must reflect the typed date.
After typing an invalid date (e.g., 2024-07-15) and pressing Tab, the datepicker element must not be visible and the form data must reflect the last valid date (2024-05-10).
Clicking outside the picker should still hide it.
Inline pickers must remain visible when their host element receives blur.
Selecting a date via the mouse grid should still update the field and hide the picker if configured.
The blur listener should not cause duplicate hide calls or errors.
The regression guard 'Type a valid delivery date and Tab away' must hold with form-data reflecting the typed valid date.
